Galaxies with zero instantaneous SFR, and those below the lowest sSFR bin, are in the lowest row and count as quenched; near the resolution limit (about 60 to 300 star particles) this probably inflates the quenched share at low mass, most visibly in Astrid (not verified against a resolution test). Stellar mass is the total bound mass, not an aperture mass; SFR is the instantaneous SFR of all gas in the subhalo.

provenance.citation: Villaescusa-Navarro et al. 2021, ApJ 915, 71 (CAMELS), cosmic-variance set, Subfind catalogues; counts by this project
provenance.extractionMethod: scripts/ingest_camels_distributions.py (HTTP range requests of the arrays; counts per seed in data/ensembles/camels-distributions.json)

records.notes: Per-galaxy distribution: the median and 16 to 84 per cent band shown as a curve are derived from the counts (scripts/derive-distributions.mjs).

definitions.imfBasis: the ASTRID records already in this dataset; the CAMELS paper does not restate it
